summary: Given distinct integers, can you build an array (nums2[i] = nums1[i] or nums1[i] - nums1[j], j != i) whose elements all have the same parity?
mainInsight: The answer is always true for n >= 1: if any element is odd, turn every even element into odd by subtracting an odd element (even - odd = odd) and keep odd elements as they are; if all elements are even, keep them all.

cards.answer: Subtract an odd element from each even element (even - odd = odd)
cards.explanation: Odd elements stay as they are; each even element becomes odd after subtracting any odd element.

promptVariants: Why is the answer always True?
Handle the all-even and the mixed cases.
cards.answer: If all elements are even, keep nums2 = nums1 (all even). If some element is odd, keep the odd elements and replace each even element e with e - o for an odd o (j != i holds because e is even and o is odd, so they are different indices), giving all odd.
